market_context.summary: South Africa is the most developed e-commerce market of the three: World Wide Worx puts online retail at about R130 billion in 2025 and forecasts R159 billion for 2026, the first full year in which online is about 10% of national retail turnover. Takealot (Naspers) remains the most-used platform, but shopping is spread across on-demand grocery apps (Checkers Sixty60 alone reported R25.5 billion of sales), cross-border players (Shein, Temu), Amazon.co.za (launched 2024, Prime added June 2026) and omnichannel retailers. For mass-market hair, skin and oral care the category leaders are the health-and-beauty chains Clicks and Dis-Chem and the grocers, whose online channels are growing fast but are largely closed to automated data collection; the general marketplaces list the same brands and are far easier to integrate. Several pure-play e-tailers have left the market (Zando closed after Jumia's exit; Superbalist was sold by Takealot), so every record below was checked for live trading on 2026-11-26.

key_facts.fact: Online retail in South Africa was about R130 billion in 2025 and is forecast at about R159 billion in 2026 (+22.5%), reaching 10% of national retail turnover in 2026 on a nominal like-for-like basis.

Platform usage among online shoppers (survey-based usage shares, not sales shares): Takealot 35.3%, Shein 21.5%, Checkers Sixty60 15%, Amazon 12.7% (World Wide Worx 'Online Retail in South Africa 2026'; its consumer research is Ask Afrika's Target Group Index, 23,910 interviews, January-December 2025).

The Competition Commission's Online Intermediation Platforms Market Inquiry (final report 31 July 2023) found that Takealot has 'a dominant share of overall online sales in South Africa'; no percentage was published in the coverage retrieved. Dated (more than 18 months old).
Checkers Sixty60 sales rose 34.5% to R25.5 billion in the 52 weeks to 28 June 2026, about 9.4% of Shoprite group turnover.

Takealot Group gross merchandise value rose 14% to about US$2 billion in the year to 31 March 2026; Takealot.com revenue was US$906 million and the group reported its first full-year adjusted EBIT profit (US$11 million).

Cross-border purchases were 18.6% of South African e-commerce transactions (about 19 million platform orders) in 2025; the R500 de minimis import concession was removed in November 2024 and cross-border growth slowed to 7% in 2025.

Most-visited retail websites from South Africa in October 2026 (Semrush estimates): temu.com 15.91M visits, takealot.com 10.51M, checkers.co.za 9.97M, bash.com 9.48M, shoprite.co.za 7.07M, shein.com 6.90M, makro.co.za 5.84M, clicks.co.za 5.27M, woolworths.co.za 4.73M, superbalist.com 4.69M, dischem.co.za 4.65M, pnp.co.za 3.56M. amazon.co.za is not in Semrush's retail list but its own Semrush page shows 11.19M visits, 85.48% from South Africa.

Clicks reports market shares of 43.8% in skincare, 32.8% in haircare and 22.7% in personal care for its 2025 financial year (all retail channels, not online only; the measurement source is not stated on the page).
South Africa had 51.7 million internet users (79.6% penetration) at the end of 2025; TikTok's adult advertising reach was 29.1 million and Facebook's 27.9 million.

ranking_method_note: weighted_score = 0.20 x ecommerce_significance + 0.25 x beauty_category_relevance + 0.20 x consumer_reach + 0.15 x brand_competitor_coverage + 0.20 x data_integration_feasibility, each scored 1-5, rounded to 2 decimals. priority_rank orders platforms by weighted_score within the country (1 = highest); ties are broken by beauty_category_relevance, then consumer_reach, as the rubric requires. Where platforms were still tied, ecommerce_significance, then data_integration_feasibility, then name were used (our addition; the rubric stops earlier). Scores are analyst judgements anchored to the evidence note beside each score. Anchors for brand_competitor_coverage (thirteen reference brands): 5 = at least 11 confirmed with real depth, or every brand tested when at least 8 were tested; 4 = 8-10 confirmed, or 11+ confirmed with thin listings; 3 = 4-7 confirmed; 2 = 1-3 confirmed; 1 = none found. Where a catalogue could not be read at all the score is a placeholder marked UNVERIFIED: 3 (neutral) for pharmacies, grocers and general marketplaces that normally stock the category, 2 for delivery apps and classifieds, 1 for cross-border value or fashion platforms and private messaging. competitor_presence.level follows the same evidence: high = score 4-5, medium = 3, low = 1-2, unknown = placeholder. Anchors for data_integration_feasibility: 5 = documented seller API plus openly readable pages, 4 = openly readable pages or feeds, 3 = partly readable or seller-portal access only, 2 = automated access refused, 1 = app-only, login wall or CAPTCHA. Closed platforms therefore rank lower for reasons of access, not commercial weight. For South Africa this mainly affects Clicks, Dis-Chem and Checkers Sixty60, which are more important to the category than their rank suggests.

platforms.name: Takealot
platforms.beauty_relevance_note: A brand search for 'nivea' returned 900 results with category facets Beauty (577) and Health (487); all major mass-market skin, hair and oral-care brands tested were listed. Garnier's South African site runs a 'Shop Black Friday with Takealot' banner, L'Oreal Paris's South African site has a 'Shop on Takealot' button and Dark and Lovely's Africa site links to Takealot product pages, so brand owners already treat it as a core e-retail partner.
platforms.pharmacy_relevance_note: A Health category exists, but no evidence of a pharmacy or dispensing service was retrieved in this session.
platforms.market_importance_note: Estimate: rests on the highest survey usage share (35.3% of online shoppers), about US$2bn group GMV, top Similarweb e-commerce rank and the regulator's 2023 dominance finding.

consumer_reach_evidence.claim: Used by 35.3% of South African online shoppers, the most-used platform. ESTIMATE: survey usage share, not a sales share.
takealot.com received 12.52M visits worldwide, 83.95% (10.51M) of them from South Africa (Semrush estimate).

Takealot Group GMV rose 14% to about US$2bn (group figure, includes Mr D); Takealot.com revenue US$906m with GMV +15% and orders +18%; the TakealotMore loyalty programme accounted for 27% of platform GMV.
Ranked #1 Ecommerce & Shopping website in South Africa (Similarweb).

The Competition Commission found that Takealot has 'a dominant share of overall online sales in South Africa'. VERIFIED source type (regulator inquiry), but no percentage appears in the coverage retrieved; dated (2023).

competitor_presence.note: Verified on 2026-11-26 by rendering Takealot's public search pages (default headless browser, no login) and reading the brand filter. Listing counts under each brand filter: Nivea 374, Colgate 172, Vaseline 152, Dove 110, L'Oreal 107, Garnier 99, Himalaya Wellness 78, Pantene 61, Dark and Lovely 42, Dabur 36, Head & Shoulders 16, Sensodyne 16. Sunsilk is UNVERIFIED (no Sunsilk brand filter appeared).

platforms.product_coverage_note: Twelve of thirteen target brands confirmed with brand-level listing counts across skin, hair and oral care. Result pages show price, promotions (for example Black Friday and TakealotMORE deals), ratings and regional stock flags (Cape Town, Durban, Johannesburg).

api_availability.note: Takealot Seller API (OpenAPI definition version 2.0) with offers, stock, sales and order endpoints; requires an API key generated in the Seller Portal and covers only the seller's own offers and sales. No public catalogue or pricing API for other sellers' listings was found, so competitor listings, prices and reviews would come from public web pages.

platforms.data_collection_feasibility_note: Documented seller API for own listings and sales, and public search pages rendered without login or a bot challenge in this session. Site terms of use were not reviewed and should be checked before any automated collection.

ecommerce_significance.note: Most-used online platform (35.3% of online shoppers) with about US$2bn group GMV.

beauty_category_relevance.note: Deep beauty and health catalogue and brand-owner campaigns, although the category leaders overall are Clicks and Dis-Chem.

consumer_reach.note: About 10.5M monthly visits from South Africa (Semrush) and the highest survey usage share.

brand_competitor_coverage.note: 12 of 13 target brands confirmed with listing counts.

data_integration_feasibility.note: Public, documented Seller API plus openly rendering public pages.

platforms.priority_rationale: Ranks first on every criterion except category leadership: largest audience, widest verified brand coverage and the only local marketplace with a documented seller API. Start here.
platforms.confidence_note: Usage, traffic and GMV come from three independent source types and brand presence was verified directly on the platform. The regulator's dominance finding is from 2023 and has no published percentage.
